label: yes
controls_available: Full-mode mouse pointerdown on the visible body arrows: slide left, slide right, morph taller, and morph wider.
Pointerup, pointercancel, or window blur releases the body hold to neutral COAST; the target mechanic has no keyboard handler.
CERTIFY and NEW ROOM are administrative controls; they are not outcome-affecting puzzle controls.
autonomous_processes: The requestAnimationFrame loop advances the simulation to elapsed 40 ms ticks even when no new agent event arrives.
Each tick applies gravity to vy and bottom, resolves solid collisions and landings, and marks the parcel fallen when it passes the room floor.

Horizontal velocity persists between input events and is damped by drag while x continues to move; morphology and contact with shelves change which states remain clear, and visible seal contact changes the collected set.
grouped_control_modes: full body_hold: all visible directional body holds, with slide-left/slide-right and morph-taller/morph-wider as the action choices
full release/coast: the neutral [0, 0] state after pointer release or cancellation
administrative certify/new-room actions, excluded from outcome-affecting D

clause_i.reason: Take D to be all full body_hold occurrences, not a hand-picked interval. The L3 island generator randomizes center, gap, opening, and well and independently mirrors the entire room. Thus two histories can have the same I_t (same prior controls and task times) while the visible landing/opening is on opposite sides or the parcel has different contact-derived x, h, and vx. The delayed-optimal slide or morph choice differs, so no policy q using only I_t can be optimal for every history in C_Delta(D).

clause_ii.reason: The canvas visibly renders every solid, seal, and the current parcel rectangle, including its x, bottom, and area-preserving width/height; the three chronological frames across the configured 80 ms window expose the parcel's displacement and direction. Together with I_t's current hold/release, that bounded trajectory window is sufficient to estimate momentum, project the state four ticks (160 ms) ahead, and choose the appropriate body arrow or brake/release action.

clause_iii.reason: The same coasting/momentum process supplies the strict loss. In an exact seed-0 replay, a reachable under-shelf state is approximately x=871.6, bottom=420, h=89, vx=4 with the first three seals collected. A=[0,1] (morph taller) can then unfold through the opening and collect the last seal. With no new action for tau=120 ms (three ticks), the parcel coasts to approximately x=881 and the next height substep is blocked by the right shelf; the same A loses its immediate action advantage. The state is still active and can be rescued by braking left and re-entering the opening, so C_Delta remains nonempty. This loss is caused by visible spatial/contact evolution, not by a deadline or merely by waiting for an enabling animation.

common_visible_process: Use D=full body_hold with the parcel coasting between a release and the next body-arrow action, Delta=160 ms (four 40 ms physics ticks), and w=80 ms (the configured three-frame window). The visible parcel trajectory under drag, together with gravity and shelf/gap contact, predicts whether a delayed slide or morph will still fit. In the under-shelf receiving opening, rightward drift moves the parcel out of the clearance needed to morph taller; at the supported-to-unsupported crossing, the same drift can also remove the horizontal bridge and lead to an irreversible fall. Recent frames reveal this process, q cannot reconstruct it from its own action clock, and g can select the delayed control from the visible trajectory.

pre_run.reason: The exact L3 generator has no separate prepare/start boundary: every instance starts active at x=center, bottom=420, h=80, vx=vy=0 with no seals collected. A neutral autonomous run leaves the parcel on the starting island at h=80; seal 0 is at y=420-reach=260 above its initial top y=340, while the other seals are displaced across the gap, landing, and opening. Reaching all four therefore requires outcome-affecting slide or morph controls during the run. The defined pre-run threshold is not met; no percentage is asserted.

source_evidence.claim: Difficulty 3 is the island profile with 240-unit island, 80-120 gap, 100-120 opening, 80 clearance, 160 reach, drag 0.85, and 90 well clearance; full interaction is implemented and the observation window is 80 ms with three frames.
The environment exposes a frame window and mouse/keyboard action types, with the runner using 180 seconds, 80 ms steps, and three frames.
The selected condition supplies the difficulty parameters; L3 generates a randomized and optionally mirrored island, gap, shelves, opening, four seals, and an active zero-velocity initial parcel.
The visible simulation preserves area, applies morphology, drag-based horizontal velocity, gravity, collision/landing, seal contact, falling, and solved/timeout status.

The browser renders solids, seals, and the parcel on canvas; tick advances from elapsed time; body controls set visible full-mode holds; release sets neutral coast; and requestAnimationFrame keeps ticking.
The full-mode body controls are a visible positioned button grid over the canvas, and the interaction buttons are native visible controls.
The authoritative replay uses the same substepped physics, validates the full interaction source and transcript, and accepts only a solved replay with matching final physical state.
Verification loads the exported result and the Concertina Courier independent grader, so the outcome is based on the replay rather than client collection claims.
The reference controller repeatedly reads the visible simulation state, predicts short-horizon motion, and changes shape/position for the L3 island, under-shelf, and opening sequence.

The frozen definition requires one common visible autonomous process satisfying clauses (i)-(iii), and the pre-run threshold overrides only when at least half of generated instances can finish after preparation without further outcome-affecting actions.
